mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on both Team A's shots FOR (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) and shots AGAINST (RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) being simultaneously above their long-run means. This is a joint two-observable condition, not a single-observable band.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both a team's recent shots-FOR and shots-AGAINST are jointly elevated above long-run levels, total match shots-on-target rises relative to matches where only one dimension is elevated.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's shot-volume surge in recent matches (shots FOR and AGAINST both elevated in RECENT_5 vs ALL_PRIOR) co-occurs with a simultaneous improvement in shots-on-target FOR, suggesting a joint recent-form regime where both attacking output and defensive exposure are jointly elevated. The relationship to test is whether matches where a team's recent shots-FOR and shots-AGAINST are both above their long-run averages produce higher total shots-on-target counts than matches where only one or neither is elevated.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots FOR and shots AGAINST) both deviating from their long-run means simultaneously. It cannot be reduced to a single observable with one coarse band, nor to a simple recent-vs-long-run split on one observable.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B's shots-FOR RECENT_5 being above ALL_PRIOR AND Team B's shots-on-target-AGAINST RECENT_5 being below ALL_PRIOR. This is an asymmetric cross-observable joint condition across the two sides.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's recent shot volume rises but the opponent's recent shots-on-target-allowed falls, the attacking team's shots-to-shots-on-target conversion rate is suppressed relative to matches where both move in the same direction.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B shows a pronounced asymmetry between its recent shots-FOR surge (RECENT_5 well above ALL_PRIOR) and its shots-on-target-AGAINST improvement (RECENT_5 below ALL_PRIOR). This cross-observable asymmetry — one team's attacking volume rising while the opponent's defensive exposure on target falls — tests whether the conversion rate (shots-on-target FOR relative to shots FOR) is jointly modulated by both teams' recent form trajectories simultaneously.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves an asymmetric joint relationship across two distinct observables (shots FOR for one team, shots-on-target AGAINST for the other), which cannot be reduced to a single observable mirror or a single-observable band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Split by half: condition on second-half period only. Jointly examine Team A's goals-against in the second half alongside Team A's cards_2h FOR (cards received in second half). The joint within-half conditioning on two distinct observables is the novel structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: In matches where a team's second-half card accumulation is elevated, second-half goals-against rises further above the first-half goals-against baseline, suggesting a compounding relationship between disciplinary pressure and defensive exposure within the second half.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A concedes substantially more goals in the second half than the first half (1H goals-against mean ~0.747, 2H ~1.089), while also accumulating more cards in the second half (cards_2h FOR ~1.468). The joint relationship between second-half defensive fragility (goals-against 2H) and second-half card accumulation (cards_2h FOR) tests whether teams that are both defensively exposed and disciplinarily pressured in the second half show a compounding effect on second-half goals-against beyond what either observable alone predicts.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires a within-half (second half) joint conditioning on two distinct observables (goals-against and cards_2h), not a single observable split by one coarse band. The half-level resolution and the two-observable joint structure together make it irreducible to the covered class.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the half (first vs second) jointly for both teams simultaneously: compare Team B's corners-FOR by half against Team A's corners-AGAINST by half. The joint cross-team half-level structure — where one team's 2H corner production rises while the opponent's 2H corner-against falls — is the novel conditioning.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's second-half corner production rises above its first-half level while the opponent's second-half corners-allowed falls below its first-half level, total second-half corners are suppressed relative to what the sum of each team's individual half-splits would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half corner-kick production (2H mean ~2.641) is notably higher than its first-half production (~2.410), while Team A's second-half corners-against (~2.442) is lower than its first-half corners-against (~2.623). This cross-team, cross-half asymmetry in corner-kick dynamics tests whether the joint condition of one team's second-half corner surge meeting the opponent's second-half corner-against suppression produces a non-additive total corner outcome in the second half.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This jointly conditions on half-level splits for two teams simultaneously across the same observable, creating a cross-team within-half interaction that cannot be reduced to a single team's observable with one coarse band or a simple home/away split.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on venue (this is a home fixture for Team A, away for Team B) and simultaneously examine two distinct observables: Team B's fouls-FOR (which is elevated away) and Team A's yellow-cards-FOR (which is elevated away). The joint two-observable, two-team venue interaction is the novel structure.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When the away team's foul production is elevated above its home-venue level and the home team's yellow-card accumulation is also elevated above its home-venue level, total match yellow cards rise above what either team's individual venue-split average would predict additively.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B commits substantially more fouls away (~13.553) than at home (~11.850), while Team A's yellow-card rate is higher away (~2.103) than at home (~1.750). The joint relationship between Team B's away foul-rate elevation and Team A's away yellow-card-rate elevation tests whether matches where the away team's foul production and the home team's card accumulation are both above their home-venue baselines produce a non-additive total disciplinary outcome, beyond what each team's venue split alone would predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) across two teams simultaneously, with venue as a shared conditioning dimension. It is not reducible to a single observable with one venue band, nor to a simple mirror of the same observable.
